issues.legal_issue: Statutory interim maintenance allowances paid while compensation for the loss of a property interest is being determined are income rather than capital receipts when they are distinct from the compensation.
material_facts: Payments called interim maintenance allowances were made under a regulation after the Jagir’s income began to be collected by the government and before the commutation terms were determined.
The allowances were recurring and measured by reference to current Jagir income, while the separate commutation sum was calculated by reference to annual revenue.
The regulations treated the allowances as ending when the terms of commutation were determined and distinguished them from the commutation sum.
The allowances compensated for the loss of income during the interim period, rather than for the loss of the Jagir itself.
issues.conclusion: Interim maintenance allowances that do not form part of the commutation amount are income and liable to tax.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Income-tax Act, 1922, the character of the receipts is determined from the regulations creating them. Sections 10, 11 and 14 of the Hyderabad (Abolition of Jagirs) Regulation, 1358F, and sections 3, 4 and 7(2) of the Hyderabad Jagirs (Commutation) Regulation, 1359F, distinguish recurring interim allowances from the capital commutation sum. The Court applied Commissioner of Income-tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co. (recurrence and regularity as characteristics of income) and approved the analysis in Commissioner of Inland Revenue v. Butterley & Co. Ltd., under which statutory interim payments may be sui generis income-compensation, arising from the statute rather than from property, investment or the right to compensation.

rule.if: income_tax_classification_proceeding and statutory_interim_allowance and recurring_payment and allowance_compensates_interim_income_loss and not part_of_commutation

predicates.income_tax_classification_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a receipt is taxable as income.
predicates.statutory_interim_allowance: A statute creates a payment described as an interim maintenance allowance pending determination of compensation.
predicates.recurring_payment: The payment is made regularly or recurs over an interim period.
predicates.allowance_compensates_interim_income_los: The payment compensates the recipient for income lost during the interim period.
predicates.part_of_commutation: The payment forms part of the separate sum paid to compensate for the loss of the underlying property interest.

issues.definition: When a tax-classification proceeding concerns a recurring statutory interim allowance that compensates for interim income loss and is separate from commutation, the allowance is taxable income.

issues.legal_issue: A sum paid as final commutation for the loss of a property interest is capital rather than income.
material_facts: The regulations provided for a separate commutation sum calculated as a multiple of the Jagir’s basic annual revenue.
The parties did not dispute that the commutation sum was paid as compensation for the loss of the Jagir.
The commutation sum was distinct from the recurring interim allowances, and any allowance paid for a period after commutation became payable was to be recovered by deduction from the commutation sum.
issues.conclusion: Payments towards the commutation amount are capital receipts and are not liable to tax as income.
issues.legal_principle: The Income-tax Act, 1922 distinguishes income receipts from capital compensation. Sections 3 and 4 of the Hyderabad Jagirs (Commutation) Regulation, 1359F, provided for the commutation sum, and section 7(2) treated payment of that sum as final commutation and provided for recovery of certain later interim payments from it. The Court distinguished the commutation sum from the interim payments, applying the distinction reflected in Commissioner of Inland Revenue v. Butterley & Co. Ltd.; it also referred to Shanmugha Rajeswara Sethupathi v. Income-tax Officer, Karaikudi, without needing to determine the precise date on which the Jagir was taken away.

predicates.income_tax_classification_proceeding: The proceeding concerns whether a receipt is taxable as income.
predicates.payment_is_commutation_sum: The payment is the final sum fixed under a scheme for commutation of the recipient’s rights.
predicates.payment_compensates_for_extinguished_pro: The payment compensates the recipient for property rights that have been extinguished.

issues.definition: In a tax-classification proceeding, a payment that is a commutation sum compensating for extinguished property rights is not taxable income.

issues.legal_issue: The nature of payments made after the point when commutation becomes payable must be determined before deciding whether those payments are taxable interim allowances or non-taxable commutation sums.
material_facts: Several payments were made after the date from which the regulations treated commutation as final.
The record did not establish whether those later payments were interim allowances for a relevant period or payments towards the commutation sum.
The tribunal had directed an inquiry into the nature of those payments, and the High Court approved that direction.
issues.conclusion: The inquiry into the nature of the later payments was proper; payments towards commutation are not income, while interim allowances that do not form part of the commutation amount are taxable income.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7(2) of the Hyderabad Jagirs (Commutation) Regulation, 1359F, treated commutation as final from the specified effective point and provided for recovery from the commutation sum of interim allowances paid in respect of a later period. The Court applied the distinction between income allowances and capital commutation sums, relying on the principles in Commissioner of Income-tax v. Shaw Wallace & Co. and Commissioner of Inland Revenue v. Butterley & Co. Ltd.

predicates.appellate_tax_classification_proceeding: The proceeding is an appeal or review of a tax-classification determination.
predicates.payment_made_after_commutation_effective: A payment was made after the point at which the governing scheme treats commutation as effective.
predicates.payment_character_is_unresolved: The record does not establish whether the payment was an interim allowance or part of the commutation sum.

issues.definition: In an appellate tax-classification proceeding, when a payment made after commutation becomes effective cannot be identified from the record as an allowance or commutation, its character requires factual inquiry.
